tools.name: net_pay
tools.description: South Korea take-home pay for an employee: monthly net salary after national pension, health and long-term care insurance, employment insurance, and withheld income tax (2026 NTS simplified withholding table) plus local income tax.

tools.name: social_insurance
tools.description: South Korea four major social insurances (national pension, health, long-term care, employment) for a monthly wage: employee deductions and employer contributions at 2026 rates.

tools.name: severance_pay
tools.description: South Korea statutory severance pay (toejikgeum): 30 days of average wage per year of service, with retirement income tax, from hire date, last working day and last 3 months of pay.

tools.name: retirement_income_tax
tools.description: South Korea retirement income tax on a severance payment: service-year deduction, converted-pay deduction, national and local tax, and the reduced tax if received as an IRP pension.

tools.name: annual_leave
tools.description: South Korea paid annual leave under the Labor Standards Act: days currently available, remaining days, next accrual, and payout value of unused leave.

tools.name: unemployment_benefit
tools.description: South Korea unemployment benefit (job-seeking allowance, silup geupyeo): daily amount with 2026 cap and floor, number of benefit days, and total.

tools.name: parental_leave_benefit
tools.description: South Korea parental leave benefit from employment insurance, month by month with caps, including the 6+6 both-parents scheme and single parents.

tools.name: weekly_holiday_pay
tools.description: South Korea weekly holiday pay (juhyu sudang): the paid weekly rest allowance owed to workers contracted for 15+ hours a week, with weekly and monthly pay including it.

tools.name: wage_conversion
tools.description: Convert between hourly wage, monthly salary and annual salary the South Korean way (monthly hours include paid weekly holiday hours, 209 for a 40-hour week), with a 2026 minimum wage check.

tools.name: minimum_wage_check
tools.description: Check a South Korean monthly wage against the 2026 minimum wage (KRW 10,320/hour): counts base pay, monthly regular bonus and cash welfare allowances, supports the 90% probation rate.

tools.name: part_time_pay
tools.description: South Korea part-time (alba) monthly pay from an hourly wage and schedule, including weekly holiday pay, after either 3.3% withholding or the four social insurances plus income tax.

tools.name: overtime_pay
tools.description: South Korea overtime, night and holiday work premiums under the Labor Standards Act (1.5x overtime, +0.5x night, 1.5x/2x holiday); workplaces with fewer than 5 employees get no premium.

tools.name: ordinary_wage
tools.description: South Korea ordinary wage (tongsang imgeum): hourly and daily ordinary wage from base pay, fixed allowances and regular bonuses, the basis for overtime, unused leave and dismissal notice pay.

tools.name: average_wage
tools.description: South Korea average wage (pyeonggyun imgeum): daily average over the 3 months before the last working day, the basis for severance pay and unemployment benefit; falls back to the ordinary wage when that is higher.

tools.name: gross_from_net
tools.description: Reverse South Korea take-home pay: the gross monthly and annual salary needed to reach a target monthly net pay after 2026 social insurance and withheld income tax.

tools.name: freelancer_withholding
tools.description: South Korea 3.3% business-income withholding for freelancers (3% income tax + 0.3% local tax), in either direction: net from gross, or the gross to invoice for a target net.

tools.name: daily_worker_tax
tools.description: South Korea daily (day-labor) worker tax: income tax after the KRW 150,000 daily deduction and 55% credit, local tax and employment insurance, for wages paid daily or in one lump sum.

tools.name: other_income_tax
tools.description: South Korea other-income (gita sodeuk) withholding of 22% on income after deemed expenses, e.g. lecture fees, manuscript fees and prizes, with the KRW 50,000 exemption threshold.

tools.name: dismissal_notice_pay
tools.description: South Korea dismissal notice allowance: 30 days of ordinary wage owed when an employer gives less than 30 days notice (not owed for under 3 months of service).

tools.name: shutdown_allowance
tools.description: South Korea business shutdown allowance (hyueop sudang): 70% of average wage, or the ordinary wage if that is lower, for days the employer suspends work (5+ employee workplaces).

tools.name: maternity_leave_pay
tools.description: South Korea maternity leave pay for 90 days (120 for multiple births): split between employer and employment insurance, with the 2026 monthly cap of KRW 2.2 million.

tools.name: paternity_leave_pay
tools.description: South Korea spouse (paternity) childbirth leave pay for the 20 paid days, and how much employment insurance covers at priority-support companies.

tools.name: reduced_hours_childcare_benefit
tools.description: South Korea reduced working hours for childcare benefit: monthly employment-insurance top-up (first 10 reduced hours at 100%, rest at 80%, with caps) plus the reduced employer pay.

tools.name: year_end_tax_settlement
tools.description: South Korea year-end tax settlement (yeonmal jeongsan) estimate for employees: refund or additional tax from gross salary, dependents, card spending and the main deductions and credits, choosing itemized vs standard credit.

tools.name: monthly_rent_tax_credit
tools.description: South Korea monthly rent (wolse) tax credit at year-end settlement: 17% or 15% of up to KRW 10 million rent for homeless tenants earning up to KRW 80 million.

tools.name: card_income_deduction
tools.description: South Korea credit card income deduction for year-end settlement: deduction from credit, debit/cash, traditional market/transit and culture spending above 25% of salary, with limits and estimated tax saved.

tools.name: pension_savings_tax_credit
tools.description: South Korea pension savings and IRP tax credit: 16.5% or 13.2% (incl. local tax) of contributions up to KRW 9 million, and the extra refund from filling the remaining limit.

tools.name: bonus_tax
tools.description: South Korea tax withheld on a bonus or incentive payment: income tax by the simplified-table bonus method over the payment period, local tax and employment insurance, and the net bonus.

tools.name: vat
tools.description: South Korea 10% VAT: split a VAT-inclusive total into supply amount and VAT, or add VAT to a supply amount, with Korean rounding.

tools.name: brokerage_fee
tools.description: South Korea real-estate brokerage fee ceiling (bokbi) for a sale, jeonse or monthly-rent lease of a house or officetel: statutory rate bracket, fee cap and VAT.

tools.name: jeonse_wolse_conversion
tools.description: Convert between South Korean jeonse deposit and monthly rent (wolse) at a conversion rate, with the statutory 4.5% cap check on a landlord's asked rent.

tools.name: child_benefits
tools.description: South Korea government cash support for a newborn: first-meeting voucher, parent benefit for ages 0-1 and the monthly child allowance up to age 9, with a dated schedule.

tools.name: business_days
tools.description: South Korea business days: count working days between two dates, or find the date N business days later, skipping weekends and Korean public holidays (2025-2027 table incl. substitute holidays).

tools.name: deposit_interest
tools.description: South Korea bank deposit or installment-savings interest after tax: maturity amount with simple or monthly-compounded interest and the 15.4% interest withholding tax (or 9.5% preferential, or tax-free).

tools.name: korean_age
tools.description: Korean age calculation: international age (the legal standard in South Korea since June 2023), year age, traditional counting age, zodiac animal, and the next birthday.

tools.name: pyeong_conversion
tools.description: Convert between square meters and pyeong, the Korean real-estate area unit (1 pyeong = 400/121 m2, about 3.3058 m2).

tools.name: pregnancy_due_date
tools.description: Pregnancy due date and gestational week from the last menstrual period, with the South Korean labor-law dates that follow: reduced working hours in pregnancy, earliest maternity leave start, and the paternity leave deadline.

tools.name: service_period
tools.description: Length of service at a South Korean employer from the hire date: years, months, days, next anniversary, annual leave entitlement for the current year of service, and severance pay eligibility.

tools.name: gift_tax
tools.description: South Korea gift tax (jeungyeose) on a gift received: relationship deduction (spouse 600M, parent to adult child 50M, to minor 20M, other relatives 10M), 10-year aggregation, marriage/childbirth deduction, 10-50% progressive rates, generation-skipping surcharge and the 3% on-time filing credit.

tools.name: housing_acquisition_tax
tools.description: South Korea acquisition tax when buying a home: 1-3% by price (sliding rate between 600M and 900M), 8%/12% heavy rates for multiple homes and corporations, plus local education tax and rural special tax, and the first-home relief of up to 2M.

tools.name: vehicle_tax
tools.description: South Korea annual vehicle tax (jadongchase) for a private passenger car: per-cc rate by engine displacement, 30% local education tax, age reduction from the 3rd year (5% a year, up to 50%), flat amount for electric cars, and the 2026 annual-prepayment discount.

tools.name: income_tax_from_tax_base
tools.description: South Korea comprehensive income tax from a tax base (gwase pyojun): the 8-bracket 6-45% progressive table with deduction amounts, plus 10% local income tax, marginal and effective rates.

tools.name: loan_repayment
tools.description: Loan repayment schedule summary as used by South Korean banks: equal monthly payment (wolligeum gyundeung), equal principal (wongeum gyundeung) or interest-only with bullet repayment; monthly payment, first and last installments, total interest.

tools.name: early_repayment_fee
tools.description: South Korea early loan repayment fee (jungdo sanghwan susuryo): repaid amount x fee rate x remaining days / fee period (usually 3 years, after which the fee is waived).

tools.name: inheritance_shares
tools.description: South Korea statutory inheritance shares and forced-heirship reserve (yuryubun) under the Civil Code: heirs by rank (children, then parents, then siblings), the spouse 50% add-on, and reserved portions (1/2 of the share for children and spouse, 1/3 for parents, none for siblings). tools.name: housing_subscription_score
tools.description: South Korea housing subscription points (cheongyak gajeom, max 84) for private apartment sales: homeless period (max 32), dependents (max 35) and subscription account period (max 17). The spouse-account bonus is not included.

tools.name: litigation_stamp_fee
tools.description: South Korea civil lawsuit filing costs: court stamp fee (injidae) from the claim amount by bracket, 1.5x on appeal and 2x at the Supreme Court, 10% off for electronic filing, plus the prepaid service-of-process fee (songdallyo).

tools.name: late_payment_interest
tools.description: South Korea statutory late-payment interest (jiyeon sonhaegeum) on a money debt: 5% civil, 6% commercial, 12% under the litigation-promotion act after a complaint is served, or a contract rate, prorated by day.
